subject: Post-demo: dedicated capacity validation experiment plan + SLO gating
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@orionlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: dedicated capacity validation experiment plan + SLO gating

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Thanks for walking through OrionLytics' expected load and latency targets; this thread is my recap and a concrete experiment plan so we can validate a Dedicated sizing that meets your SLOs before committing to reserved capacity.

Quick summary of what we heard on the call:
- Target P95 token latency: <= 120ms for interactive streaming responses (90% of calls include streaming).
- Sustained peak throughput: 9M tokens/min during batch overnight windows, with 600 concurrent streaming sessions during business hours.
- Typical prompt+generation length: 1200 input tokens, 800 output tokens average.
- Model family: open Llama-2-style family (quantized variants acceptable); preference to avoid full FP16 unless needed.

Proposed experiment (2 weeks total):
1) Baseline microbench: run 24h token-per-second benchmarks across candidate GPU configs (A100 80GB, H100 80GB, L40S) using a sampled production prompt set.
2) Streaming stress window: emulate 600 concurrent streams at 2–3RPS/session with average 800-token outputs and measure P50/P95/P99 tail across 1s, 5s, 30s buckets.
3) Concurrency/throughput sweep: sweep reserved throughput from 50k to 250k tokens/sec and measure latency vs cost curve.
4) KV/prefix cache validation: validate prefix caching for repeated prompts reduces backfill token work by at least 25% for your NLU flows.

Deliverables:
- GPU fit matrix (latency & cost-per-1M tokens) for each candidate card.
- Recommendation for reserved throughput and concurrency limits to hit 95% of requests P95 <= 120ms with 99.9% availability.
- Small-run runbook & dashboard (we'll share a read-only dashboard link).

Attachments: I attached a short SLO checklist, a GPU comparison matrix template, and the experiment runbook draft.

Immediate asks for your team:
- Confirm the numbers above or correct any assumptions (especially average output token sizes and concurrent session target).
- Share a sample of 500 representative prompts (anonymized) we can use for the microbench.
- Any procurement constraints / lead times we should be aware of.

Next internal step: Ben and Rishi — can you confirm estimated test capacity and whether we need additional quota to spin up H100-backed Dedicated nodes for the sweep?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: slo_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), gpu_comparison_matrix.csv (csv), experiment-runbook.md (markdown)
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@orionlytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orionlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: dedicated capacity validation experiment plan + SLO gating

Irene — thanks, this looks good and thorough. A few clarifications from our side: 
- P95 target: yes, <= 120ms for interactive streaming is the hard SLO; P99 can be softer but we'd like to quantify tail behavior.
- Concurrency: 600 is conservative; business-day peak could spike to ~800, but sustained periods are usually 15–30 minutes.
- Output tokens: 800 avg is accurate; we do have long-report tails (~3–4k tokens) for ~5% of calls — we can flag those and route to a non-interactive path.

We can share anonymized prompts; I'll send a 500-sample set by EOD tomorrow (Jul 1). Procurement: lead time for a reserved contract is ~4–6 weeks once we have a sizing recommendation — procurement looped here.

Couple of asks for Redwood: 
- Can you include an explicit validation that streaming fallbacks (to smaller quantized variants) preserve latency under 150ms while maintaining acceptable quality?
- We need an initial cost estimate ballpark (monthly) for the recommended reserved throughput / GPU profile to present to finance.

If this plan works, we'll aim to schedule the first microbench window next week.

—Alex
Alex Wu
Head of Platform Engineering, OrionLytics
alex.wu@orionlytics.com

On Wed, Jun 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@orionlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: dedicated capacity validation experiment plan + SLO gating

Thanks — quick tech notes:
- For streaming P95 <= 120ms with 600–800 concurrent streams, H100 with 80GB or A100-80 are the primary candidates; L40S is lower-cost but the tail may suffer on 4k outputs.
- We'll run two variants: 1) H100 baseline at reserved throughput X (TBD) and 2) quantized Llama-2-13B int8 on A100 to test cost-optimized path with streaming fallbacks.
- Need to ensure our KV cache has enough memory per shard; recommend reserving 10% extra KV capacity during the sweep to avoid eviction noise affecting latency.

Operational asks for the run:
- Orbit team (ops) kickoff to grant temporary increased cluster quota for the H100 run (Irene: can you request this once Alex confirms test window?).
- Rishi: can you prepare a quick perf script that emits streaming chunks with realistic inter-chunk timing to mimic client-side buffers. I'll add script to experiment-runbook.md.

I'll also produce a quick heatmap table (latency vs concurrency vs reserved tps) after the baseline microbench.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@orionlytics.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: dedicated capacity validation experiment plan + SLO gating

Alex — thanks for the prompt sample set; received and started vetting the prompts. Two quick notes from validation prep:
- We'll flag the 3–4k-token tails and run them in a separate batch so they don't skew the interactive streaming SLA measurements.
- For the streaming fallback test, we'll implement a split routing policy: route initial 90% tokens to the high-precision variant and for tokens beyond a 1.5k threshold switch to quantized variant to simulate graceful degradation.

Logistics: Ops has approved a temporary H100 quota for next Tue/Wed (Jul 6–7) assuming Alex confirms a 2-hour window each day. Irene — can you confirm with Alex and procurement which block they'd prefer?

I'll capture all results in the shared drive, and Ben will publish the heatmaps + cost table.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Platform Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Attachment references: experiment-runbook.md (contains test scripts), gpu_comparison_matrix.csv
